resolutions.researcher_notes: Oil & Gas Online, 2001-07-30 (syndicating a Falcon Gas Storage Company press release): 'Falcon Gas Storage Company and its subsidiary, Hill-Lake Gas Storage, L.P., today announced that right-of-way acquisition has been completed for the construction of a new 17-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline in Eastland County... Construction is scheduled to start the first week of August on the pipeline, which is expected to be operational by November 1 [2001]... When completed, Falcon's Hill-Lake Pipeline will operate at a maximum pressure of 1200 psig.' That establishes the pipeline as operational from late 2001. PRNewswire's 2021-02-17 release for Tailwater Capital LLC (a distinct, later publisher) confirms NorTex Midstream Partners -- the current owner, successor to Falcon's Hill-Lake Gas Storage LP -- 'operates the largest portfolio of non-utility gas storage facilities in North Texas' with 'a Bcf of depleted reservoir working gas capacity, 83 total miles of natural gas transportation pipelines' still in active service as of 2021, continuously led by the same management (CEO John Holcomb, who was Hill-Lake's own VP of Marketing on its 2014 FERC/RRC filings). NorTex's own facilities page (current site now redirects to Williams; confirmed via Wayback capture dated 2020-11-26, live origin blocked to automated fetchers) independently lists 'Hill-Lake Gas Storage' among its active facilities with a working FERC/RRC-filed Statement of Operating Conditions still posted. Two distinct publishers (Oil & Gas Online, trade press, and PRNewswire/Tailwater Capital, a different company entirely) agree the pipeline has been in continuous operating status from 2001 through at least 2021 -- so tier high/independent true. Automated substring screen failed only because the sources render the name with a hyphen ('Hill-Lake Pipeline'/'Hill-Lake Gas Storage') rather than the sheet's unhyphenated 'Hill Lake Pipeline'; I read all three documents directly and confirmed the value.

Oil & Gas Online (2001) describes the project as 'a new 17-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline.' Independently, Hill-Lake Gas Storage LLC's Statement of Operating Conditions as filed with FERC (July 2014, PDF; live origin 403s, Wayback capture read directly with pdftotext) is captioned 'STATEMENT OF OPERATING CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO NGPA SECTION 311 SERVICE ... of HILL-LAKE GAS STORAGE, LLC' and describes it throughout as 'an intrastate underground natural gas storage facility' interconnected via the pipeline to 'Atmos' Line X Pipeline and the North Texas Pipeline,' both natural-gas transmission systems. Two distinct publishers (a trade-press outlet and the company's own federal regulatory filing) agree the commodity is natural gas -- tier high/independent true.

Oil & Gas Online, published 2001-07-30, reporting Falcon Gas Storage Company's own announcement: 'right-of-way acquisition has been completed for the construction of a new 17-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline... Construction is scheduled to start the first week of August on the pipeline, which is expected to be operational by November 1.' This is a contemporaneous (same-year) news account dating the construction start to August 2001, matching the sheet's ConstructionYear=2001 exactly. I searched FERC eLibrary, the Texas Railroad Commission's public permit/GIS resources, and EIA's historical pipeline-projects dataset for an independent second source giving a construction date for this specific 17-mile lateral (as distinct from the Hill-Lake storage field itself, which the field's SOC filings describe only in service-conditions terms, not construction history) and found none -- FERC has no jurisdiction over this intrastate line (Hill-Lake is NGA-exempt per its own SOC, 'operating an intrastate underground natural gas storage facility... exempt from the jurisdiction of [FERC]'), and RRC's public permit index is not full-text searchable for a 2001-era pipeline of this type without an operator/permit number I could not otherwise obtain. Single origin (the Falcon Gas Storage press release, as syndicated by this one trade outlet), so medium/independent:false rather than overclaiming.

Same Oil & Gas Online article: 'a new 17-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline in Eastland County' -- exact match to the sheet's LengthKnown=17.00/LengthKnownUnits=mi. I looked for a second, independent source with this specific figure (FERC eLibrary -- not applicable, line is FERC-exempt/intrastate; RRC pipeline permit data -- not accessible without an operator/permit id; EIA historical pipeline-projects table -- does not carry a Hill-Lake/Falcon 2001 lateral; PHMSA/NPMS -- mileage not broken out per-lateral in public summaries I could reach) and did not find one, so this stays medium/independent:false rather than overclaiming to high.

Same Oil & Gas Online article, same sentence: '...a new 17-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline...' -- exact match to the sheet's Diameter=20/DiameterUnits=in. No independent second source with this specific figure was found (same search as the Length unit above); medium/independent:false.

Oil & Gas Online (2001): 'a new 17-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline in Eastland County near Dallas/Ft. Worth' -- Eastland County is in north-central Texas. Independently, Hill-Lake Gas Storage LLC's own Statements of Operating Conditions filed with BOTH the Texas Railroad Commission and FERC (July 2014, PDFs read via Wayback + pdftotext) repeatedly define the facility and its points of receipt/delivery as 'located in Eastland County, Texas' ('Hill-Lake's Facility located in Eastland County, Texas'; 'Point(s) of Delivery... located on Hill-Lake's system in Eastland County, Texas'). Both endpoints of this short connector pipeline are within Eastland County, Texas, United States, matching the sheet's StartState/Province=Texas, StartCountryOrArea=United States, EndState/Province=Texas, EndCountryOrArea=United States. The RRC and FERC SOCs are the same company's own filings (one origin between them), but Oil & Gas Online is a distinct, independent trade-press publisher agreeing on the same county/state -- tier high/independent true.
